description: Barley Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with barley flour, cooked on a medium-hot tawa — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Take a barley flour in a mixing bowl add pinch of rock salt (if desired) and mix well. Gradually add water and knead into soft and smooth dough (use warm water for kneading to obtain soft rotis) cover the dough and rest it for 15-20min.
Make equal sized ball into dough and dust each ball with a little quantity of flour and roll it into thin, round roti.

Heat a tawa on medium flame and place the rolled roti on it and apply ghee, cook until small bubbles appear then flip the roti and cook the other side by applying the ghee and gently press with spatula for the roti puffs up (put ghee on to the roti, if desired).
Serve hot with curry or dal or chutney.

description: Blackgram Stuffed Paratha (Vedanika) is an Ayurvedic stuffed flatbread made with wheat flour, de-husked black gram and sesame oil, dust and roll thin — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Soak the de-husked black gram for 6-8hrs or overnight then grind it in a mixer to obtain a smooth paste.
Take wheat flour in a mixing bowl add pinch of rock salt (if desired) and mix well. Gradually add water and knead into soft and smooth dough cover the dough and rest it for 15-20min.
Make equal sized balls from the paste for the filling purpose and divide the dough into equal portions, flatten a dough ball place the paste in the centre and seal edges.

Dust a little quantity of flour and roll it into thin and round roti. Heat a tawa on medium flame and place the rolled roti on it and apply ghee or sesame oil, cook until small bubbles appear then flip the roti and cook the other side by applying the ghee or sesame oil. Cook until golden brown spots appear and serve hot with ghee (if desired) and any side dish of your choice.

prepAheadNote: Soak de-husked black gram 6–8 hr or overnight.

description: Blackgram Stuffed Puri (Vadori) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour and black gram, heated ghee in a deep pan — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Soak black gram for 6-8hrs or overnight then grind it in a mixer to obtain a smooth paste.
Take wheat flour in a mixing bowl, gradually add water and knead into soft and smooth dough.
Make equal sized balls from the paste for the filling purpose and divide the dough into equal portions,
Flatten a dough ball place the paste in the centre and seal edges. Apply a little oil and roll it into thin and round roti.
Heat ghee in deep frying pan. Once the ghee is hot gently slide a rolled poori into the ghee.
Press lightly with a slotted spoon to help it puff up the flip and fry until both sides become golden brown.
Remove and drain excess ghee on a paper towel and serve hot with any side dish of your choice.

description: Black Gram Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with black gram flour, roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Take black gram flour in a mixing bowl add pinch of rock salt (if desired) and mix well. Gradually add water and knead into soft and smooth dough cover the dough and rest it for 15-20min.
Make equal sized ball into dough and dust each ball with a little quantity of flour and roll it into thin, round roti.

Heat a tawa on medium flame and place the rolled roti on it and apply ghee, cook until small bubbles appear then flip the roti and cook the other side by applying the ghee and gently press with spatula for the roti puffs up (apply ghee, if desired).
Serve hot with curry or dal or chutney.

description: Wheat Roti is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour and milk, roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Take wheat flour in a mixing bowl, gradually add milk and knead into soft and smooth dough. cover the dough and rest it for 5-10min.
Make equal sized ball into dough and dust each ball with a little quantity of flour and roll it into thin, round roti.

Heat a tawa on medium flame and place the rolled roti on it and apply ghee, cook until small bubbles appear then flip the roti and cook the other side by applying the ghee and gently press with spatula for the roti puffs up (apply ghee if desired).
Serve hot with curry or dal or chutney.

description: Baati (Angarakarakati) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with wheat flour, divide into medium balls — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take wheat flour in a mixing bowl add pinch of rock salt (if desired) and 3-4tsp. of ghee mix well. Gradually add water and knead into firm dough. Cover the dough and allow it to rest for 15-20 min.
Divide the dough into equal portions and make a medium sized round ball. Place these balls over the coal embers or a wire rack above the charcoal
OR Bake in a preheated oven at 1800C for 25-30 min.
OR use Air fryer by smearing the paper with oil and then place the balls on to the paper for 15 - 20 mins.
OR use preheated pressure cooker for 10 min, with a layer of salt or sand at the bottom of a cooker. Place the wheat balls on a rack and cook on low flame for 30-40min. turning occasionally.
OR use thick bottomed pan over low flame gas stove turning occasionally, once partially cooked, roast them directly over a low flame for a few min. to achieve golden brown colour.
Remove the cooked balls from heat and allow them to cool slightly, then dip it in melted ghee or pour ghee generously over it and serve with dhal.

description: Classical Soft Bread (Samita Roti / Mandaka) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with refined wheat flour (samita), roll into thin, round rotis — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala.

steps.text: Take Refined wheat flour in a mixing bowl, gradually add water and knead well to make soft and smooth dough. cover the dough and rest it for 5-10min.
Make equal sized ball into dough and dust each ball with a little quantity of flour and roll it into thin, round roti.

Heat a tawa on medium flame and place the rolled roti on it and apply ghee, cook until small bubbles appear then flip the roti and cook the other side by applying the ghee and gently press with spatula for the roti puffs up.
It should be served with milk, ghee and rock sugar.

description: Barley Savory Discs (Kulmasha) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with barley flour, hot water and mustard oil, shape into small round discs (2–3 inches) — a classical recipe from Kaiyadeva Nighantu. Barley (Yava) balances Kapha and Pitta and is prized in Ayurveda for its lightness.

steps.text: Take barley flour in a mixing bowl, add required amount of rock salt and mustard oil. Gradually add sufficient hot water and knead well to form a smooth dough.
Shape the dough into small, round discs (2-3 inches) and steam them until fully cooked.
Once done, remove from heat.

description: Vada (Vataka) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with de-husked black gram, wet ginger paste and hingu (asafoetida), heated oil over medium flame — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Wash de-husked black gram thoroughly and soak in water up to 4-6 hrs after that drain the water and grind the dal into smooth and thick batter by using required quantity of water and beat the batter until it becomes light and fluffy.
Then add required quantity of rock salt, wet ginger paste and hing and mix the batter well.
Heat the oil in deep frying pan over medium flame. Wet the hands with water, take a small quantity of batter and shape it into vada by make a hole in the centre.
And carefully slide the vada into the hot oil deep frying until the both side of the vada becomes golden brown and crisp.
Then remove and drain the excessive oil and serve with any side dish of your choice.

description: Pumpkin Crunch Bites (Kushmanda Vataka) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with black gram flour, pumpkin paste and wet ginger paste, heated oil over medium flame — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Take Black gram flour in mixing bowl and add rock salt, wet ginger paste, hing, black pepper, fenugreek seeds and cumin seeds and add pumpkin paste and mix it well and gradually add water to make smooth and thick batter. beat the batter until it becomes light and fluffy.
Heat the oil in deep frying pan over medium flame. Wet the hands with water, take a small quantity of batter and shape it into vada by make a hole in the centre.
And carefully slide the vada into the hot oil deep frying until the both side of the vada becomes golden brown and crisp.
Then remove and drain the excessive oil and serve with any side dish of your choice.

Raghunathasurivirachita Bhojanakutuhalam Edited with English Translation, Notes and Illustrations by Scholars of the Centre for Theoretical Foundations (CTF), I-AIM(2012) Bhaksha Prakarana P.No :49

description: Puri (Purika) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with refined wheat flour, gram flour (besan) and cumin seeds, deep-fried in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both… — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala.

steps.text: Take equal quantity of Refined wheat flour and Gram flour in a mixing bowl add cumin seeds, hingu, black pepper powder mix well then add 2-3tsp. of ghee mix well then gradually add water and knead well to make soft and smooth dough.
Make equal sized ball from the dough. By Appling little quantity of ghee / oil to the ball make ball into thin and round roti shaped purika.

Heat ghee in deep frying pan. Once the ghee is hot gently slide a rolled purika into the ghee / Oil. Press lightly with a slotted spoon to help it puff up the flip and fry until both sides become golden brown.
Remove and drain excess ghee on a paper towel and serve hot with any side dish of your choice.

description: Masala Puri (Candarika / Ghrtapura) is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with rice flour, green gram flour and black gram flour, deep-fried in hot ghee until puffed and golden on both… — a classical recipe from Bhojana Kutuhala. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Take equal quantity of all the above-mentioned flour in a mixing bowl add cumin seeds, hingu, black pepper powder mix well then add 2-3tsp. of ghee mix well then gradually add water and knead well to make soft and smooth dough.
Make equal sized ball from the dough. By Appling little quantity of oil to the ball make ball into thin and round roti shaped purika.
Heat ghee in deep frying pan. Once the oil is hot gently slide a rolled purika into the Oil.
Press lightly with a slotted spoon to help it puff up the flip and fry until both sides become golden brown.
Remove and drain excess ghee on a paper towel and serve hot with any side dish of your choice.

description: Karpura Crispy Sticks (Karpuranalika) is an Ayurvedic fritter made with wheat flour / samita, clove powder and edible camphor (karpura), deep-fried in ghee until golden and crispy — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take a wheat flour / Samita in to a mixing bowl then add adequate quantity of water and ghee to knead it into a smooth dough.
Shape the dough into small, elongated, tubular forms (3-5cm).
For the preparation of filling, powder the ingredients like clove, pepper, Karpoor and rock sugar and mix together,
Carefully stuff the little amount mixture inside the tubes, seal both ends securely by gently pressing the both edges and deep fry the filled tubes in ghee until they become golden and crispy.

description: Stuffed Cottage Cheese Dumplings (Dugdha Kupika) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with cow's milk, lemon juice and rice flour, **Make chena:** Boil milk — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Cow's milk (Dugdha) builds Ojas — the body's vital essence.

steps.text: Prepare Chena (Cottage cheese) :
Boil 500 ml cow’s milk
Add 10 ml lemon juice gradually while stirring until the milk curdles
Strain through a muslin cloth and wash with clean water to remove sourness
Hang for 20-30 min. to drain excess water.
Prepare the Dough :
Transfer the prepared chena to a bowl.
Add 10 gm rice flour
Knead for 8-10 min. until a smooth, crack-free dough is obtained.
Shape the Dumplings :
Divide the dough into 3-4 equal portions (about 25-30gm each)
Roll into smooth balls.
First frying :
Heat ghee over medium flame
Deep-fry the balls until light golden brown
Remove and allow them to cool slightly
Stuffing :
Make a small cavity in the centre of each fried ball.
Fill with a small amount of the reserved chena
Seal the opening carefully using a little dough
Second frying :
Fry the filled dumplings again until golden brown and fully cooked
Remove and drain excess ghee
Sugar syrup :
Dissolve 20 gm sugar in 40 ml water
Boil until a 1-2 thread consistency is reached
Add a tiny pinch of edible camphor
Final step :
Immerse the fried dumplings in the warm sugar syrup for 10-15 min. and serve warm.

description: Pumpkin & Big Beans Sweet Pancake is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with ripe pumpkin, chopped, cowpeas / soybeans and ragi flour, add ragi paste to the cooked pumpkin — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Soak ½ cup of cowpeas / soybeans for 4 hrs. after that cook well in pressure cooker then add 1 cup of small pieces of ripe pumpkin and cook further with a glass of water.
Then take a bowl with a cup of water and add 30gm of ragi flour stir it well to form a smooth paste and to avoid lumps.
Add this ragi paste into the cooked pumpkin vessel and boil for few min, keep stirring then add 15 gm of jaggery syrup, 30 gm of grated coconut and 10 ml of ghee and mix well.
Take another pan heat it on medium flame and lightly grease it with butter / ghee. then pour a prepared batter on pan and spread it gently, cook it well and the edges begin to set.
Flip carefully and cook the other side until it turns in to golden brown. And serve hot with any side dish of your choice.

description: Green Gram & Fenugreek Chila is an Ayurvedic flatbread made with green gram sprouts, chopped fenugreek leaves and ginger, heated a flat pan — a classical recipe from AYUSH.

steps.text: Take a mixer grinder and add the green gram sprouts and a small piece of ginger grind it smooth like batter consistency,
Then add 1 cup of chopped fenugreek leaves, 2 teaspoon of Bengal gram flour and salt as per taste to the batter, mix it well and rest it for the 15 min.

After that heat up the flat pan lightly grease it with oil. Pour a ladleful of batter onto the centre of tawa and spread it in a circular motion to form a thin, cook until the chila becomes crispy. And have it with any side dish of your choice.

description: Fresh Fenugreek Stir Fry (Methika) is an Ayurvedic preparation made with methi (fenugreek) leaves and hingu, boiled in water 3–5 min until soft — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take methi leaves and clean well with water
Now boil the leaves in water up to 3-5min (until properly boiled) and squeeze it properly to make lump/mass.
Take a clean pan and add ghee and heat it, then add hingu,   boiled methi mass and rock salt as per taste and roast it properly.

description: Punjabi Greens is an Ayurvedic preparation made with dark green leafy vegetable, ghee / oil and cumin seeds, heated oil — a classical recipe from Morningstar.

steps.text: Wash the green leafy vegetable of your choice thoroughly with water, then chop.
Take a pan add oil and heat it on medium flame then add cumin seeds, turmeric and hingu to it.
Add garlic paste, chopped onion(optional) fry till the onion turns into the golden brown colour.
After that add chopped green leafy vegetable and cook over medium heat until it is cooked properly and rock salt is an optional with proper quantity.

sources.text: Morningstar — Ayurvedic Cooking for All, 3rd repr. 2011

description: Brinjal Fry is an Ayurvedic preparation made with brinjal, lemon juice and hingu, heated oil — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam.

steps.text: Take brinjal wash it thoroughly and cut them into thin slices.
Heat the oil in a pan, Cook sliced brinjal in medium flame, stir it  occasionally.
Fry until the brinjal becomes soft and crispy on edges after that add hingu, ginger paste and rock salt as per taste and cook another 2-3 min. then switch off the flame,
Add lemon juice to it and mix it well
Cover and leave it for 3-5min. and garnish with coriander leaves before serving it.

description: Parval Fry (Patola) is an Ayurvedic preparation made with pointed gourd (parval) and hingu, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take a pointed gourd wash it thoroughly and cut them into thin slices.
Heat the ghee in a pan. Fry sliced patola(pointed gourd) in medium flame, stirring occasionally.
Then add hing, Rock salt and as well as other spices that you want for the taste with proper quantity and cook dry on moderate fire until it becomes soft
Once it is evenly cooked switch off the flame, cover it for 3-5min.
Serve the dish when it is hot to enjoy the flavour.

description: Smoky Eggplant Delight is an Ayurvedic preparation made with eggplant, mustard seeds and cumin seeds, heated oil — a classical recipe from Gowans.

steps.text: Wash and slice eggplant into small pieces, sprinkle with salt and wait until eggplant sweats. Wash off salt and dry.
Heat oil in pan and pop the mustard seeds, follow with cumin seeds, curry leaves and then onion and stir.
Once the onion become transparent add the turmeric. Add eggplant closed the lid until it cook soft then add salt as per taste. Have it as a side dish.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Smoky Golden Delight is an Ayurvedic preparation made with sliced pumpkin, sliced almonds and mustard seeds, steamed pumpkin cubes until soft — a classical recipe from Gowans. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Cut the pumpkin into small sized cubes and cook them on steam.
Take pan add ghee heat it after that pop the mustard seeds then add cumin seeds, curry leaves and Chopped onion fry till the onion turns to golden colour.
Take another pan and fry the sliced almonds till it turns to golden brown.
Then add Steamed pumpkin sliced to the pan fry it well. Then add roasted almonds to it and add turmeric powder and salt as per the taste.
Mix all together perfectly and close the lid for 3-4 min. then switch off the flame and have it.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Sweet Aloo Sauté is an Ayurvedic preparation made with chopped pumpkin, chopped sweet potato and mustard seeds, steamed pumpkin and sweet potato until soft — a classical recipe from Gowans. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Steam the chopped pumpkin and chopped sweet potato until they become soft.
Take a pan add ghee heat it on medium flame.
Then add mustard seeds, cumin seeds, curry leaves, chopped onion, ginger paste and turmeric powder fry them properly.
Add steamed vegetables to the pan add rock salt as per taste mix it all together properly and closed the lid for 2-3min. then have it.

sources.text: Gowans — Food for Life: Ayurvedic Recipes, 2009

description: Gooseberry Stir Fry is an Ayurvedic preparation made with indian gooseberry (amla), sesame oil and curry leaves, heated sesame oil — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Amla (Amalaki) is the supreme rasayana, balancing all three doshas.

steps.text: Wash the Amla thoroughly and dry well, cut and remove seeds.
Take a pan add sesame oil and heat it on medium flame add amla pieces fry well.
Add curry leaves, pepper powder, turmeric powder, salt, hing and mix well. Then have it as side dish.

description: Ginger Barfi (Ardraka Paka) is an Ayurvedic halwa made with fresh ginger, jaggery and dry ginger powder, cooked jaggery until a thick syrup forms — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Take a pan add jaggery, cook till a thick syrup is formed. Then add grated ginger, stir and cook for 5-7 min. on low flame.
Add ghee and mix well, cook for another 5-10 min. now add the powder of all above ingredients and cook for another 5-10 min.
If you want sesame seeds, then add it 2-3tsp. it is optional and spread the content on plate greased with ghee.
Let it cool before cutting in pieces in any shape. When cooled, store in an air tight container. It remains for about a month.

description: Coconut Laddu (Narikela Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with grated coconut, milk and rock sugar powder, cooked grated coconut in milk until well cooked — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Coconut cools, rejuvenates and nourishes all seven tissues.

steps.text: Take a cup of graded coconut in a pan and add milk and cook well
Take required quantity of ghee in another pan and then this cooked material is roasted in ghee properly.

Take another pan for the preparation of sugar syrup, take sugar as per desired quantity of sweetness and add proper quantity of water now boil it until it forms proper consistency for the binding purpose
Then add roasted graded coconut into sugar syrup and also add cardamom powder and dry ginger powder as required quantity and make small laddus out of it.
It can be stored till 5 to 7 days
Enjoy it like a snack and when required

description: Sweet Coconut Momo (Bhaimi) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with wheat flour, grated coconut and dry grapes, **Filling:** Heat ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Preparation of dough – Take a cup of wheat flour add ghee and add required amount of water kneaded well to make it soft dough.

Preparation of stuff – Take ghee in pan, heat it and add graded coconut, dry grapes, chopped kharjura, required quantity of sugar powder then add aromatic powder roast well in a medium flame and make it as paste for the stuffing purpose.
Divide the dough into small balls, roll each ball into a thin circular wrapper.
Place filling in the centres. Fold and pleat the edges to seal it properly.
Then fry deeply in the ghee with mild fire until it turns into golden brown.

description: Urad Amrut Laddu (Masha Ladduka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with de-husked black gram, rock sugar powder and aromatic powder, **Boondi:** Heat ghee — a classical recipe from Ksemakutūhalam. Black gram (Masha) builds strength and nourishes the tissues.

steps.text: Batter preparation:

Soak a de-husked black gram in water for 4-6hrs. after that drain the water, grind with small quantity of fresh water added gradually. Grind until the batter is soft enough and is having pouring consistency.
Boondi preparation :

Heat the ghee in a deep pan, hold a boondi ladle/Perforated spoon over the ghee and pour a little batter onto the ladle and gently tap it so that small droplets fall into the ghee and deep fry them until cooked but not crispy. Remove and drain excess oil.
Sugar syrup preparation :
In a pan add sugar and water heat until the sugar dissolves and forms into syrup consistency. Add aromatic powder to it and mix it well.
Laddu preparation :

Now add the ghee fried boondi to the hot sugar syrup mix well so that the boondi absorbs the syrup and also add ghee roasted dry fruits to it.  once it attained a desirable consistency make laddus out of it by taking a desirable amount, if the mixture is dry, sprinkle a little warm syrup /water to make good consistency.

description: Wheat Balls (Godhuma Laddu) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with wheat flour, jaggery and cardamom powder, heated ghee — a classical recipe from ICMR-NIN. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take a ghee in a pan and once the ghee becomes hot add wheat flour and roast well in a medium flame.
Take another pan add jaggery as desired quantity of sweetness and add a sufficient quantity of water and boil it to make a proper consistency of jaggery syrup for binding purpose.
Once the syrup is prepared turn off the flame then slowly add roasted wheat flour stir continuously to avoid the lump once it mixes well then add cardamom powder and dry ginger powder mix it well.

Once it attained a desirable consistency, make laddus out of it by taking a desirable amount, if the mixture is dry, then add a desired quantity of ghee or sprinkle a little warm syrup /water to make good consistency.

steps.text: Take a cup of refined wheat flour in a mixing bowl add 2-3tsp. of melted ghee mix well, add water gradually and knead gently to make a soft and smooth dough.
Then divide the dough into small portions and make them into smooth, crack free balls.
Take a pan and heat the ghee on medium flame then slowly add the balls into ghee, fry the balls slowly until they turn golden brown on all sides then remove the balls and drain excess ghee.
Take another pan and prepare the sugar syrup with 1tsp. of aromatic powder, Once the syrup prepared turn off the flame
Once these balls cools to moderate temperature then transfer the balls into the warm sugar syrup.
Allow them to soak for 2-3 hrs so that they absorb the syrup well.

description: Date Laddoo (Kharjur Laddoo) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with dates (kharjur), cashews and almonds, lightly roast nuts in 2 tsp ghee until golden — a classical recipe from AYUSH. Coconut cools, rejuvenates and nourishes all seven tissues.

steps.text: Separate seeds from the dates and cut in small pieces. Cut the cashew and almonds also in small pieces and slightly roast in the pan with 2 spoons of ghee.
After that mix the kharjur pieces in pan and make small sized laddoos and roll it over the grated coconut.
Roasted sesame seeds may be used instead of grated coconut.

description: Sweet Vermicelli Balls (Sevika Modaka) is an Ayurvedic sweet ball made with fine wheat flour (samita) and rock sugar, heated ghee — a classical recipe from Bhavaprakasha. Ghee (Ghrita) kindles digestion and carries nutrients deep into the body.

steps.text: Take a mixing bowl add flour and ghee mix thoroughly and add sufficient water to prepare a smooth dough.

Heat the ghee in a deep pan, hold a boondi ladle/Perforated spoon over the ghee and pour a little batter onto the ladle and gently tap it so that small droplets fall into the ghee and deep frying them until crispy and golden.
Once fried, immerse them in sugar syrup (one thread consistency) for proper absorption.
Once soaked, remove the strands from sugar syrup and prepare small balls/ modaka as desired.

Jaggery and rock sugar are considered cleaner sweeteners than refined sugar in Ayurveda.

steps.text: Take flour milk and ghee, mix together to prepare thin batter.
Cook the batter over low heat, once half cooked add the ghee
And continue cooking until it reaches thicker consistency.
Remove from the fire, place the mixture in a cool place and add an equal amount of sugar, mix thoroughly, and prepare small balls.
